memory_update.text: VECO is the strongest US-listed underfollowed candidate for the compound-semiconductor epitaxy/process-tool node because it has disclosed $250M+ of InP laser manufacturing equipment orders tied to optical interconnect demand.
AIXNY/Aixtron should remain a reference leader for MOCVD arsenide/phosphide tools, but verify US OTC listing, liquidity, and current market-cap bucket before using it in later dashboard layers.
LITE and COHR are not pure equipment plays but are essential demand anchors: their InP laser and 800G/1.6T optical capacity ramps validate tool demand for Veeco and Aixtron.

Need next-layer search for smaller metrology, in-situ epitaxy monitoring, specialty materials, precursor, wafer, and inspection suppliers tied to MOCVD/InP laser yield; these may be more obscure than the direct toolmakers.

node: Compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools for lasers and optical connectivity
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools for AI optical connectivity. The clearest direct equipment exposure is Veeco, with Aixtron as the key OTC/foreign-listed reference toolmaker. Lumentum and Coherent are included as direct laser/optics customers and capacity-expansion anchors rather than pure tool vendors. The underfollowed lane is strongest at the equipment layer because MOCVD, ion-beam coating, wet processing, and InP laser manufacturing tools sit one step below the more visible 800G/1.6T transceiver and AI networking beneficiaries.
